clue.text: Receiving signal, criminal stamped in frustration

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the words that follow are twisted out of order
receiving means taking something inside, so one piece is held within the others

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange
to point is to signal or indicate

explanation.surface: A crook, getting a signal, stamps their foot in exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'in frustration', but it belongs to the letters being rearranged; the shuffled STAMPED IN then wraps round POINT to give DISAPPOINTMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointment is the feeling of being thwarted when hopes go unmet, a close synonym of frustration.

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: a duty is a task or job
an EP (extended play) is a type of record

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a second job while keeping records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as an adjective, but here it is a noun: a second is an assistant, as in a duel or boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is a second-in-command, the person who stands in for or assists the main officeholder.

blocks.note: first meaning: noticed or caught sight of
second meaning: covered in spots or pimples

explanation.surface: Someone is seen with a bad case of acne.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted is both the past participle of spot, meaning noticed, and an adjective for skin marked with pimples.

blocks.note: a prop is a support
agate is a banded semiprecious stone

explanation.surface: A jeweller spreads a mount around a semiprecious gem.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate an idea or plant is to spread or disseminate it.

indicators.note: unusual suggests an odd arrangement, so the following word's letters are rearranged
toting means carrying, so the first word holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: just in the sense of merely
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is just carrying an unusually heavy load on a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the fly means improvising it as you go, without preparation.

clue.text: Arm going up to win gold

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: a gun is a firearm, an arm
to get is to win or obtain

explanation.surface: An athlete raises an arm to claim gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a lump of native gold, so the word stands for gold by example.

clue.text: No longer ready for German philosopher to be announced

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so we want a word sounding like the philosopher's name

blocks.note: Karl Marx, the German philosopher

explanation.surface: A German philosopher says he is no longer ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash; the Deutschmark was Germany's money until the euro replaced it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks were German currency, ready money, until the euro arrived in 2002, so they no longer circulate as cash.

blocks.note: neon is a vivid, glowing shade
ate as in 'what's eating you?', meaning troubled

explanation.surface: A garish paint job has made an expectant parent anxious about the nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, a baby in its first weeks.

clue.text: Style of music unknown in support of The Cure?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so these pieces come below the first

blocks.note: taken as written
rap is a style of music
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A music style and an unknown act are supporting the band The Cure on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cure is a British rock band, which makes 'support' look like an opening act; the question mark flags that a cure is only one thing therapy offers.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal, so a cure is what it aims at; the question mark covers the looseness.

clue.text: Dance arranged at school with zero publicity

blocks.note: a prom is a formal school dance
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A school dance was organised with no publicity at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a promotional item or campaign, a short word for publicity.

indicators.note: something tangled is knotted up, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A biplane's wheel got its rim snagged in something.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Tiger Moth is a 1930s British biplane used for training pilots.

clue.text: Four aliens returned without a word

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the letters run right to left
without here means outside, so the other letters surround the article

blocks.note: ET, the film alien, four times over
taken as written

explanation.surface: Four aliens came back without saying anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a word' reads as silence; instead 'without' is the old sense outside, and 'word' is the definition, as in 'can I have a word?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people, like having a word with someone.

blocks.note: a big name is a star, a celebrity
R is short for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a name is the best substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like 'finest', but it is Pete Best, the Beatles' drummer whom Ringo Starr replaced in 1962.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr took over the Beatles' drum stool from Pete Best, so he was literally Best's replacement.

clue.text: Team removing lead supporter by choice

indicators.note: removing the lead means taking off the front letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a side is a team
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A team drops its lead supporter as a matter of choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in the best of circumstances, what one would pick if one had the choice.

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for Australian
Sir Robert Peel was a British prime minister; the 's makes it plural-looking

explanation.surface: Australia's prime minister has withdrawn from a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an Aussie leader; the prime minister is actually Robert Peel, the 19th-century British PM, with the apostrophe-s kept as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out cold or out for the count is unconscious, as a sleeper is.

clue.text: Exotic vehicle happening to follow special ones

indicators.note: to follow means come after, so this piece goes at the end of the others

blocks.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
an ace is a one in cards or dice
happening and hip both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy foreign car comes along behind special models.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceship is a craft for travelling in space, about as exotic as a vehicle gets.

clue.text: Happiness of one in top hotel

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another word

blocks.note: to trump is to top or beat
I is the Roman numeral one
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A guest is delighted to be staying at the best hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumph is the elation of victory, a strong form of happiness.

indicators.note: something overheard is only caught by ear, so we want what the next word sounds like

blocks.note: to sand is to smooth or polish
that and which are both relative pronouns

explanation.surface: A Polish sailor overheard something about that submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb to polish; 'submarine' is the long US-style sub roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine, or sub, is a long filled roll, which is one kind of sandwich.

blocks.note: first meaning: more reckless, comparative of an adjective for hasty
second meaning: a slice of bacon

explanation.surface: A health warning about an unwise choice of breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasher is the comparative of rash, meaning more reckless, and also a thin slice of bacon eaten at breakfast.

blocks.note: first meaning: a ..., a chewy fruit candy
second meaning: one of the pins knocked down in the game of ...

explanation.definitionFit: Skittles are a brand of chewy candy, and a skittle is a bottle-shaped pin in the bowling game of that name.

clue.text: Artist probing yellowish-brown and dark brown

indicators.note: something probing pushes inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: camel is a yellowish-brown colour
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is investigating two shades of brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel names the brown colour of burnt sugar, a shade darker than camel.

indicators.note: stocking means carrying inside as stock, so the letters lie within the preceding words

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the two words

explanation.surface: A deli stops selling spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its intrinsic nature, its spirit, as in the spirit of the law.

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: S is short for small
an equine is a horse

explanation.surface: A pony is close to getting a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiner' suggests a black eye; here it is something that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin is a small glittering disc sewn onto clothing, so it is literally something that shines.

clue.text: Farm worker, lacking aid, raised millions?

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the named letters are taken out
in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the remainder reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a dairymaid works with milk cows on a farm
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A farmhand, without help, brought up millions.
explanation.definitionFit: A myriad is a countless number; millions is one example, hence the question mark.

blocks.note: first meaning: Rugby ..., one of the two codes of rugby
second meaning: an alliance or association

explanation.surface: Rugby League is named as a kind of rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Rugby League' as one phrase, the other code; split it and 'League' becomes the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby Union is the fifteen-a-side code of rugby, and a union is a league or alliance of members.

indicators.note: upturned in a down clue means turned upside down, so the short word reads bottom to top
in a down clue, the drone carries the other piece on top of it, so that piece comes first

blocks.note: taken as written
a drone is a low, continuous hum

explanation.surface: A drone carries a book upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: North Leeds transformed by Stallone forever

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: N is short for north
taken as written
Sylvester Stallone is known as Sly

explanation.surface: Sylvester Stallone has changed the north of Leeds for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Endlessly means without ever stopping, the same as forever.

clue.text: Perfume covering lake, breaking Parisian agreement

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one letter splits the word that follows

blocks.note: a patch is a covering, as over an eye or a hole
oui is French for yes
L is short for lake

explanation.surface: A scent masks a lake and wrecks a deal made in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is a heavy, musky perfume made from the oil of an Asian plant.

clue.text: Capital of Ghana losing exterior bits

indicators.note: losing the exterior means stripping off the outside letters of the country's name

blocks.note: taken as written; its first and last letters go
binary bits are 0 and 1, which look like the letters O and I

explanation.surface: Ghana's capital is losing its outlying districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Ghana' looks like a request for Accra; 'Capital' alone is the definition. A computer bit is a 0 or a 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the word before it has its letters mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to shepherd is to steer or guide

explanation.surface: A dog lies in the manger, baffling a bullock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog in the manger' is an idiom for someone spiteful, and 'steer' looks like a young bull; here it is the verb to guide.
explanation.definitionFit: The German shepherd, or Alsatian, is a large breed of working dog.
